o1.biggest_strength: It nails the three real levers in this business in the right order and gives usable message copy plus sensible ranges with mostly sound maths.
o1.biggest_mistake: It weakens the fit-finder recommendation by treating a key pre-purchase fix as only a side note instead of a main workstream tied to the 60-day plan.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the fit-finder move a first-class deliverable with a proper test plan and tighten the exchange-value maths so the commercial impact is framed more cleanly.

o2.biggest_strength: It is the most owner-aware version: it spots the real causes, uses holdouts and guardrails well, and turns them into a practical 60-day sequence with on-brand copy.
o2.biggest_mistake: It overclaims the exchange revenue impact with shaky maths that would make me mistrust the headline value.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fix the sales-kept calculation, keep all impact ranges tied to gross saving or retained gross profit, and it would be excellent.

reason: Both are strong and clearly built on the brief, but Output 1 is a bit more numerically trustworthy and cleaner on the owner’s main ask for expected savings. Output 2 has slightly better testing discipline, but the loose revenue math is a bigger fault for me.
